record_notes.DCP-LETT-2585: Five retained blocks, metadata/XML, excluded material, all footnotes and bibliography read. December 16, 1859 is after the endpoint. Thursday December 22 London visit and museum delivery are planned, stomach willing, not completed. The detailed list of pigeon drawings, skulls and lower jaws specifies intended loans; hybridism and pigeon manuscripts are also planned loans. Separate volumes beginning with domestic productions are a publishing intention; later Variation is not current knowledge. The embedded 57 Queen Anne Street address supplies routing, not a new letter or scientific content. The subsequent cancelled visit prevents treating this as a dispatch receipt.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-2600: Three retained blocks and complete metadata/XML, exclusions, notes and bibliography read. December 24 is after the endpoint. Darwin could not come to London and now sends the previously specified articles and manuscripts. This actual dispatch differs from the December 16 plan. He inspected the manuscript last night, December 23, and recommends correlated pigeon traits and the history on manuscript page 118. His defence of minute treatment is his judgment; no surviving uniquely identified incoming prompt is present. A sequence of two Darwin letters is not an incoming-to-Darwin training pair.
